\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.MajorityFourierTailAsymptotics}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Main majority Fourier level bound]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b001
}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain}
\leanok
For each natural number $k$, define the main majority Fourier level quantity to be
$(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Main majority Fourier tail bound]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierTailMain}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b002
}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierTailMain}
\leanok
For each natural number $k$, define the main majority Fourier tail quantity to be
$(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the Main Fourier Level Term]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_pos}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $k$, the quantity $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the Main Fourier Tail Term]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierTailMain_pos}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierTailMain_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.majorityFourierTailMain}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $k$, the quantity $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-level limiting weight formula]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_two_mul_add_one_eq}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002
}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_two_mul_add_one_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_eq, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $j$, the limiting majority Fourier weight at level $2j+1$
equals $\frac{2}{\pi(2j+1)}$ times the odd majority influence at index $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-Level Fourier Main-Term Identity]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_two_mul_add_one_eq}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_two_mul_add_one_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain, FABL.oddArity_rpow_neg_three_halves, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceMain}
\difficulty{5}
For every nonnegative integer $j$,
$(2/\pi)^{3/2}(2j+1)^{-3/2}=\frac{2}{\pi(2j+1)}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi(2j+1)}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Limiting majority Fourier weight error]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain}
For each natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weight error is the limiting
majority Fourier weight at level $k$ minus the main majority Fourier weight at level
$k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds on the limiting weight error]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_two_mul_add_one_eq, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_two_mul_add_one_eq, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceError, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceError_mem_Icc, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceMain}
\difficulty{5}
For every odd natural number $k$, the error between the limiting majority Fourier weight
and $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$ lies between $0$ and $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-5/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic error in majority Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError_isBigO}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightError_mem_Icc, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_pos}
\difficulty{4}
As odd integers $k$ tend to infinity, the error between the limiting majority Fourier
weight and $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$ is $O\bigl((2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-5/2}\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of a real power]
\lean{FABL.antitoneOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\label{FABL.antitoneOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real $s\le 0$, the function $x\mapsto(2x+1)^s$ is nonincreasing on
$[0,\infty)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of a negative power tail]
\lean{FABL.integrableOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\label{FABL.integrableOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,a\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $s<-1$ and $a\ge 0$. Then the function $x\mapsto
(2x+1)^s$ is integrable on $(a,\infty)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A power integral over a half-line]
\lean{FABL.integral_Ioi_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\label{FABL.integral_Ioi_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.integrableOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\difficulty{6}
Let $s,a\in\mathbb R$ with $s<-1$ and $a\ge 0$. Then
\[\int_{x>a}(2x+1)^s\,dx=-\frac{(2a+1)^{s+1}}{2(s+1)}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integral bounds for a power tail]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_add_one_rpow_tail_bounds}
\label{FABL.two_mul_add_one_rpow_tail_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.antitoneOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow, FABL.integrableOn_two_mul_add_one_rpow}
\difficulty{5}
For every real number $s<-1$ and every natural number $q$, the integral of $(2x+1)^s$
over $x>q+1$ is at most the series of its values at the odd integers beginning with
$2q+3$, and that series is at most the integral over $x>q$; explicitly,
\[\int_{q+1}^{\infty}(2x+1)^s\,dx\leq\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}(2(r+q+1)+1)^s\leq\int_q^{\infty}(2x+1)^s\,dx.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tail as a shifted infinite sum]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_shifted_tsum}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_shifted_tsum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weight above $k$ equals
$\sum_{r=0}^{\infty} w_{k+1+r}$, where $w_j$ is the limiting majority Fourier weight at
level $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-indexed tail sum identity]
\lean{FABL.shifted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_tsum_eq_odd}
\label{FABL.shifted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_tsum_eq_odd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_eq, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_hasSum_one}
\difficulty{5}
For every odd natural number $k$, the sum of the limiting majority Fourier weights from
index $k+1$ onward equals the sum over the indices $k+2(r+1)$ for $r\in\mathbb{N}$; that
is, $\sum_{r=0}^{\infty} w_{k+1+r}=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty} w_{k+2(r+1)}$, where $w_j$
denotes the limiting majority Fourier weight at index $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-level tail formula]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_tsum_odd}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_tsum_odd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_shifted_tsum, FABL.shifted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_tsum_eq_odd}
\difficulty{1}
If $k$ is an odd natural number, then the limiting majority Fourier weight above $k$
equals $\sum_{r=0}^{\infty} w_{k+2(r+1)}$, where $w_j$ is the limiting majority Fourier
weight at level $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power bounds for the odd-level tail]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_power_bounds}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_power_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.integral_Ioi_two_mul_add_one_rpow, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_tsum_odd, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_hasSum_one, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le_levelMain_mul, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain_le_limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.two_mul_add_one_rpow_tail_bounds}
\difficulty{6}
If $k$ is an odd natural number, then $(2/\pi)^{3/2}(k+2)^{-1/2}\leq T(k)\leq
(2/\pi)^{3/2}\bigl(k^{-1/2}+(1/3)k^{-3/2}\bigr)$, where $T(k)$ is the limiting majority
Fourier weight above $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power inequality for odd integers]
\lean{FABL.odd_rpow_neg_half_mul_one_sub_inv_le_succ}
\label{FABL.odd_rpow_neg_half_mul_one_sub_inv_le_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddArity_rpow_neg_one_half}
\difficulty{5}
For every odd natural number $k$, $\displaystyle k^{-1/2}\left(1-\frac1k\right)\le
(k+2)^{-1/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power identity for odd integers]
\lean{FABL.odd_rpow_neg_three_halves_eq_neg_half_div}
\label{FABL.odd_rpow_neg_three_halves_eq_neg_half_div}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddArity_rpow_neg_one_half, FABL.oddArity_rpow_neg_three_halves}
\difficulty{3}
For every odd natural number $k$, $\displaystyle k^{-3/2}=\frac{k^{-1/2}}{k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds for the odd-level tail]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_power_bounds, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain, FABL.odd_rpow_neg_half_mul_one_sub_inv_le_succ, FABL.odd_rpow_neg_three_halves_eq_neg_half_div}
\difficulty{4}
If $k$ is an odd natural number, the limiting majority Fourier weight above $k$ lies in
the closed interval with endpoints $M(k)(1-1/k)$ and $M(k)(1+1/(3k))$, where
$M(k)=(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Asymptotic majority Fourier tail bound]
\lean{FABL.abs_limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_div_tailMain_sub_one_le}
\label{FABL.abs_limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_div_tailMain_sub_one_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_mem_Icc, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain_pos}
\difficulty{5}
For each natural number $j$, set $a_j=0$ if $j$ is even and
$a_j=\frac{2}{j2^j}\binom{j-1}{(j-1)/2}$ if $j$ is odd. For every odd natural number
$k$, define $W_k=\frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{j>k}a_j$ and $T_k=(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$. Then
$\left|W_k/T_k-1\right|\leq 1/k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Relative tail error estimate]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_relativeError_isBigO}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_relativeError_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abs_limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_div_tailMain_sub_one_le, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain}
\difficulty{3}
Along the odd natural numbers as $k\to\infty$, the relative error $T(k)/M(k)-1$ is
$O(1/k)$, where $T(k)$ is the limiting majority Fourier weight above $k$ and
$M(k)=(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be an odd positive integer, and let $k$ be an even nonnegative integer. The sum
of the squared Fourier coefficients of the majority function on the $n$-dimensional
Boolean cube, over all subsets of coordinates of size $k$, is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight as a sum of levels]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAbove_eq_sum_levels}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAbove_eq_sum_levels}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAbove, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel}
\difficulty{5}
For every natural number $n$, every natural number $k$, and every function
$f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, the total Fourier weight on subsets of size greater than $k$
equals the sum of the Fourier weights at levels $j$ in the interval $k+1\le j<n+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight above a level]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAbove_boolean_eq_one_sub_sum_range}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAbove_boolean_eq_one_sub_sum_range}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeightAbove, FABL.fourierWeightAbove_eq_sum_levels, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.sum_fourierWeightAtLevel_range, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $k$ be a natural number
with $k\le n$. The total Fourier weight of its real-valued version on subsets of size
greater than $k$ equals $1-\sum_{j=0}^{k} W_j(f)$, where $W_j(f)$ is the total Fourier
weight at level $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Tail as one minus initial sum]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_one_sub_sum_range}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_one_sub_sum_range}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_hasSum_one}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weight above $k$ equals
$1-\sum_{j=0}^{k} w_j$, where $w_j$ is the limiting majority Fourier weight at level
$j$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers, with $n$ odd and $j\le n$. The limiting majority
Fourier weight at level $j$ is at most the total Fourier weight at level $j$ of the
majority function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite level majority Fourier weight bound]
\lean{FABL.finite_level_sub_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b001
}
\label{FABL.finite_level_sub_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_eq_zero_of_even, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_le_limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_eq, FABL.majority}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $j$ be nonnegative integers, with $n$ odd and $2j<n$. The Fourier weight of
the majority function on $n$ signs at level $j$, minus the limiting majority Fourier
weight at level $j$, is at most $\frac{2j}{n}$ times that limiting weight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound for a negative half-power sum]
\lean{FABL.sum_range_natCast_rpow_neg_half_le}
\label{FABL.sum_range_natCast_rpow_neg_half_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For every nonnegative integer $k$,
\[\sum_{j=0}^{k}(j)^{-1/2}\leq 2\sqrt{k},\]
where the zeroth term is interpreted using the real-power convention at zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority Fourier-weight sum bound]
\lean{FABL.weighted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_sum_le}
\label{FABL.weighted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_eq, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le_levelMain_mul, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain, FABL.odd_rpow_neg_three_halves_eq_neg_half_div, FABL.sum_range_natCast_rpow_neg_half_le}
\difficulty{5}
For every natural number $k$, the sum of $j$ times the limiting majority Fourier weight
at $j$, over $0\leq j\leq k$, satisfies $\sum_{j=0}^{k} j\,w_j\leq
4(2/\pi)^{3/2}\sqrt{k}$, where $w_j$ is the limiting majority Fourier weight at level
$j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict bound from oddness]
\lean{FABL.two_mul_lt_of_odd_of_two_mul_sq_le}
\label{FABL.two_mul_lt_of_odd_of_two_mul_sq_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
If $n$ and $k$ are natural numbers, $n$ is odd, $k>0$, and $2k^2\le n$, then $2k<n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Limiting and finite Fourier tail comparison]
\lean{FABL.limiting_tail_sub_finite_tail_mem_Icc}
\label{FABL.limiting_tail_sub_finite_tail_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.finite_level_sub_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le, FABL.fourierWeightAbove, FABL.fourierWeightAbove_boolean_eq_one_sub_sum_range, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_one_sub_sum_range, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le_finite_level, FABL.majority, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain, FABL.two_mul_lt_of_odd_of_two_mul_sq_le, FABL.weighted_limitingMajorityFourierWeight_sum_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers such that $n$ and $k$ are odd and $2k^2\le n$. The
limiting majority Fourier weight above level $k$, minus the Fourier weight above level
$k$ of the majority function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, lies between $0$ and
$4(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ and $k$ be odd natural numbers with $2k^2 \le n$. The Fourier weight of
majority on subsets of size greater than $k$, divided by $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$,
differs from $1$ by at most $5/k$ in absolute value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority Fourier Level Relative Error]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierLevel_family_relativeError_isBigO}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b001
}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierLevel_family_relativeError_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.abs_fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_div_levelMain_sub_one_le, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.majority, FABL.majorityFourierLevelMain}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ assign to each positive odd integer $k$ a natural number, and suppose that
$n(k)$ is odd and $2k^2\le n(k)$ for every such $k$. For the majority function on the
$n(k)$-dimensional sign cube, let $W_k$ be the sum of the squares of its Fourier
coefficients over all coordinate subsets of size $k$. As $k$ tends to infinity through
the odd integers, $W_k/\bigl((2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}\bigr)-1=O(1/k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority Fourier Tail Relative Error]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierTail_family_relativeError_isBigO}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b002}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierTail_family_relativeError_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.abs_fourierWeightAbove_majority_div_tailMain_sub_one_le, FABL.fourierWeightAbove, FABL.majority, FABL.majorityFourierTailMain}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ assign to each positive odd integer $k$ a natural number, and suppose that
$n(k)$ is odd and $2k^2\le n(k)$ for every such $k$. For the majority function on the
$n(k)$-dimensional sign cube, let $T_k$ be the sum of the squares of its Fourier
coefficients over all coordinate subsets of size greater than $k$. As $k$ tends to
infinity through the odd integers, $T_k/\bigl((2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}\bigr)-1=O(1/k)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd majority Fourier weight tail]
\lean{FABL.tendsto_limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_odd_zero}
\label{FABL.tendsto_limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_odd_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_eq_one_sub_sum_range, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_hasSum_one}
\difficulty{4}
For each integer $k\geq 0$, let $a_k=0$ when $k$ is even and, when $k$ is odd, let
$a_k=\frac{2}{k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$. Set $W_k=\frac{2}{\pi}a_k$ and
$T_k=\sum_{j>k}W_j$. As the integer $q$ tends to infinity, $T_{2q+1}$ tends to $0$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Suppose that for each odd natural number $k$ a natural number $n(k)$ is specified, with
$n(k)$ odd and $2k^2\le n(k)$. As $k$ tends to infinity through odd natural numbers,
both the level-$k$ Fourier weight of majority on $n(k)$ variables, divided by
$(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$ and then decreased by $1$, and the Fourier weight above level
$k$, divided by $(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}$ and then decreased by $1$, are each $O(1/k)$.
\end{theorem}
